subject: Sandbox integration playbook & SDK auth/routing next steps
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma@brightsidehealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today — sandbox & SDK clarification

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for taking the time to walk us through Redwood yesterday — that was helpful. We wanted to capture a quick recap and a few clarifying questions while they're fresh. Major items for our engineering team are below.

- Sandbox environment: we need a reproducible local dev flow for prototypes (Python + TypeScript). Is there a minimal Docker image or Compose file you recommend?
- Auth: we run behind Okta and need to understand token exchange to use Redwood Private. Do you support OIDC token forwarding or a service-account style key?
- Routing & fallbacks: if we call the hosted API, can requests be routed to a dedicated model variant when latency spikes?
- Structured output / tool calling: we have a simple set of internal tools (patient lookup, triage) — what's the recommended pattern for tool calling and safe structured outputs?
- Embeddings/rerankers: we plan to do semantic search over clinical notes. Any notes on index format, embedding size choices, and whether Redwood can host reranking on the same deployment?

Attaching the security questionnaire our procurement team asked for — placeholder answers OK for now. Also attaching a one-page outline of our PoC goals.

Next steps we propose: a short technical workshop next week (30–45m) with our engineers + yours to walk through the sandbox and auth flow.

Thanks,
Emma Park
Director of Product Engineering
BrightSide Health

Attachments: BrightSide_Security_QA.pdf, PoC_Goals_1pager.pdf
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@brightsidehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — sandbox & SDK clarification

Hi Emma — great to meet yesterday, and thanks for the clear list. Looping Marcus (infra) and Monica (solutions) for the workshop and detailed follow-ups. Below is a short playbook and proposed agenda so we can get your engineers productive quickly.

Quick answers up front:
- Sandbox: we maintain a lightweight repo with Docker + npm/pip sample apps (Python + TS). You can boot a local dev sandbox (no cloud creds) that simulates KV cache and a small model runner for request validation.
- Auth: Redwood Private supports OIDC token forwarding and short-lived service tokens. For Okta you can either: 1) configure OIDC passthrough (recommended for full identity context) or 2) use a low-privilege service account that exchanges for short-lived inference tokens. We'll send a one-page flow diagram.
- Routing/fallbacks: yes — policy-based routing can route to a cheaper quantized variant or fallback to a hosted endpoint if Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Policies are configured per-route.
- Tool calling / structured output: we support function/tool calling with JSON schema enforcement and a safety layer. Pattern: 1) declare tool schemas, 2) use structured-output mode for strict parsing, 3) run a lightweight reranker if multiple tool results need ranking.
- Embeddings & rerankers: recommended vector size is 1536 for our prebuilt clinical encoder. You can host reranking on the same Dedicated pool (we recommend isolating long-running rerankers onto a separate worker set for predictability).

Proposed 30–45m technical workshop agenda (we can split across two sessions if you prefer):
1) Local sandbox quickstart (15m) — clone repo, npm/pip install, run docker-compose, run sample Python/TS request.
2) Auth patterns & Okta mapping (10m) — OIDC passthrough vs service-account flow.
3) Routing & fallback demo (5m) — policy example.
4) Structured output + tool calling (10m) — sample schemas and safety mode.
5) Embeddings & reranking notes (5m) + Q&A.

Action items (who/what):
- Marcus: provide sandbox repo link + docker compose and a small local model container (ETA: 2027-04-11).
- Monica: prepare the one-page Okta integration flow and sample OIDC config (ETA: 2027-04-12).
- Soojin: schedule the workshop and share HubSpot/DocuSign placeholders with procurement (ETA: 2027-04-11).

Can you share a couple of time slots next week that work for your engineers? Morning PST tends to be easiest for our infra folks.

Regards,
Sooy (SoJin) Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: integration_playbook_v1.md

Thanks Soojin and team — that readout is exactly what we needed. A couple of clarifying points from our security lead:

- Data residency: for the PoC we will be using a small de-identified dataset in our US region. We may need Dedicated or VPC options later; for the sandbox PoC we just need to ensure logs do not leave the container.
- Audit logs: can you surface per-request metadata (request id, model variant, routing decision) to a S3-compatible audit store?
- Embedding retraining: we may want to fine-tune embeddings on clinical note domain data. Does Redwood provide a pipeline or recommended method for locally fine-tuning and then uploading embeddings/indexes?

Available times for a 45m session next week:
- Tue 2027-04-12 10:00–10:45 PST
- Wed 2027-04-13 09:00–09:45 PST

We prefer Tue if possible.

Best,
Emma

On attachments: the security questionnaire included a couple of items about log retention and access controls — happy to have your team fill placeholders and we can iterate during procurement.
